params.body:
## Why

A source that passes its trial waits for a person to admit it, and the Observatory looks up its terms of use first so that person only reads the sentence that was found. That lookup ran only at the end of a scout run. The scheduler starts scout when the queues are nearly empty (`raw < 20`, `classified < 10`), and with 146 trials feeding signals in they never were.

On 23 November 2026, read on the box: 85 trials had passed and waited for their terms, and none had them looked up.

## What

- `runTermsRound` in `packages/core/source-terms.mjs`: today's round, once. It writes its day to `terms_rounds` before the first lookup, so a round that is cut off is not started again that day, then looks up `TW_TERMS_PER_DAY` trials (10 by default; 0 switches it off) with the existing `prepareTerms`.
- `bin/terms-round.mjs` runs it; `--force` runs it again on the same day.
- `packages/server/terms-round.mjs`: the server starts that script once a day from 06:00 UTC, after the trial waves and before the morning desk mail, as its own process, and never two at once. Its own process because `callLLM` is synchronous: inside the server it would hold every request for as long as a page is read. The log is `~/logs/terms-round.log`.
- The scout run still looks up a few at its end. The desk's line says "a few each day".

Nothing here admits and nothing writes `terms`: what is found goes in `terms_found`, as before.

## Checked

- `test/source-terms.test.mjs`: a round looks up as many as the day allows, runs once a day, again only with force, finds nothing left the next day; at zero it is off; its day is written before the first lookup. The server's tick starts it from six, once, not while one runs, and again the next day.
- `bin/terms-round.mjs` against an empty database: runs, then skips the same day.
- Full suite 1826 of 1826, `tsc` clean.

## After merge

Nothing to run. The server checks at start, so after a deploy past 06:00 UTC the first round starts at once. At ten a day, the 85 waiting today are looked up in about nine days.
params.title: Terms of trials that passed are looked up every day
